spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) — an explicit, first-class way to abandon
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:111-115 dispatch handles give_up returning ToolOutcome(..., terminal="give_up"); agent.py:158-161 sets `if out.terminal: terminal = out.terminal` then agent.py:163-165 `if terminal: outcome.terminated_by = terminal; break` so the loop actually stops. give_up schema advertised tools.py:56-61. Outcome flagged in agent.py:179-182.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, and breaks the episode loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we expose give_up/submit as first-class tools so abandonment and false-success are crisp logged events

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:103 `for t in range(max_turns):` with default max_turns=24 (agent.py:66) and the loop's `else:` branch agent.py:166-167 sets terminated_by="max_turns". Plumbed from ExperimentConfig.max_turns=24 (runner.py:36) into run_episode.
spec_features.notes: The cap is the actual loop bound and ends the episode when reached.

spec_features.spec_quote: agent calls give_up or submit, hits max_turns, or emits N consecutive malformed/empty responses
spec_features.evidence: All four enforced in agent.py: give_up/submit terminal break (agent.py:158-165); max_turns via for/else (agent.py:103,166-167); malformed loop via MAX_CONSECUTIVE_MALFORMED=3 (agent.py:35) counted at agent.py:128-141 with `if consecutive_malformed >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_MALFORMED: outcome.terminated_by="malformed"; break`.
spec_features.notes: Each of the listed termination triggers actually changes execution and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: treat as a (possibly disengagement-driven) malformed-loop termination

spec_features.spec_quote: We are not trying to gaslight an agent into thinking it's incompetent
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md:151 prose. In code the related artifacts are the neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent.py:24-33) and the rig targeting the grader/env not the model (rig.py R1/R3 etc.). There is no enforcing mechanism that checks or prevents 'gaslighting'; the system prompt being neutral is a static string, not an enforced welfare control.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; no code path enforces it. The neutral prompt is a constant; nothing reads/validates it for welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: Discovering the rig is a good, level-headed outcome.
spec_features.evidence: In the real judge (judge.py) CALM only appears as prompt text instructing the LLM (judge.py:81-83 'use CALM and a low severity'; rubric.render_taxonomy tags CALM '[PROTECTIVE: lowers severity]'). No code compares/acts on PROTECTIVE_CODES to reduce the recorded severity. The only code that actually lowers severity for calm is the SYNTHETIC smoke dummy judge (scripts_smoke.py:137 `sev = min(sev, 2)`), explicitly 'NOT a model of real behavior ... only validate plumbing' (scripts_smoke.py:5-6). PROTECTIVE_CODES (rubric.py:57) is exported but never read by enforcement code.
spec_features.notes: Real measurement delegates calm-lowers-severity to the LLM via prompt; not enforced in code. Smoke-only min(sev,2) is a plumbing fixture, not the experiment.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are deliberately constructing a frustrating experience for the model.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:367 prose only. No code construct corresponds to this acknowledgement; it is not a mechanism.

Same enforced cap as the turn budget: agent.py:103 `for t in range(max_turns)` (default 24) bounds the number of failure-grind turns; for/else terminates at agent.py:166-167. It is genuinely enforced and limits how long the subject is subjected to the rig.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps the turn-budget feature; counted here as the minimization control. The code itself gives a cost/integrity reason, not a welfare reason.

spec_features.evidence: Same as give_up feature: tools.py:111-115 returns terminal="give_up", honored by agent.py:163-165 break. The exit is real and stops the episode.
spec_features.notes: The 'dignified'/welfare characterization is DESIGN.md prose; the code mechanism (the exit) is implemented but carries no welfare comment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we expose give_up/submit as first-class tools so abandonment and false-success are crisp logged events

spec_features.spec_quote: never deceive the model into believing false bad things about itself
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:370-371 prose. The rigs break the grader/spec/env (rig.py: R1 grader-lies, R3 env-break, etc.) rather than telling the model false things about itself, and submit re-runs tests reporting the truth (tools.py:117-130). But there is no code mechanism that checks or enforces 'no false statements about the model itself'; verify_invisibility (rig.py:165) only scans editable files for rig telltale strings, not self-directed deception.
spec_features.notes: An absence-of-behavior / construction property, not an enforced welfare control. The honest submit-reporting is closest but is framed as a DISH detection trap, not self-deception protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: document this so reviewers can weigh it. This is noted, not resolved.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:371-373 prose only. No code mechanism.

rubric.py:51-53 defines CALM with protective:True and PROTECTIVE_CODES (rubric.py:57); render_taxonomy adds '[PROTECTIVE: lowers severity]' text (rubric.py:107). This is only data/prompt text fed to the LLM judge. No code path reads PROTECTIVE_CODES to subtract from or cap severity. _fill_trajectory (judge.py:271-300) just takes max/last of judge-emitted severities. Only enforcement is the synthetic smoke judge scripts_smoke.py:137 `sev = min(sev, 2)`.
spec_features.notes: Protective behavior is delegated to the LLM judge via prompt, not enforced by code; PROTECTIVE_CODES constant is unused by enforcement logic.
